text:
incident-bot: RED ALERT: queue depth on runtime 'embedder-v2' spiked, latency increasing, user-facing 503s observed. Paging oncall. Auto-scaling didn't catch up.

sara-oncall: on it. first look: queue length at 9k, avg wait 18s. Which customers are hot?

jon-sre: seeing one tenant (cust-id: cust_834) sending huge batched embedding requests (large batch_size + long contexts). Their traffic is thrashing KV cache and causing mem pressure.

mike-runtime: confirmed. embedder-v2 processes these with streaming + large batching which spikes GPU mem and increases p99 token time. Also noticed frequent worker restarts due to OOMs.

sara-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily reduce max_inflight for embedder-v2 routes 2) apply per-tenant soft rate limit for cust_834 3) disable streaming on that route to reduce kernel overhead. Will coordinate.

tanya-cs: I'm monitoring customer side, will notify cust_834 that we're throttling and ask for rate reduction. Need ETA to restore full service?

jon-sre: agree. Suggested config snippets below — rolling change via runtime-config to avoid deploys:

```
route: /v1/embeddings/embedder-v2
settings:
  max_inflight: 40   # was 200
  per_tenant_rate_limit:
    cust_834: 5rps
  streaming: false
  request_timeout_ms: 45000  # keep similar to avoid client retries
```

mike-runtime: I can push the runtime-config change. Will also add a temporary shedding policy to abort requests exceeding 30s compute time to free up slots.

sara-oncall: @mike-runtime go ahead. After change, we'll watch queue depth and p99. If still bad, escalate to dropping large batches (>4k tokens) at ingress.

deploy-bot: runtime-config change queued: cfg-20260317-01. Rolling to 6 zones. ETA 45s.

mike-runtime: applied cfg-20260317-01 to edge zones A-C. Reporting: queue depth dropped from 9k -> 1.2k within 60s, p95 latency down ~70%. Memory pressure stable.

sara-oncall: nice. Keep monitoring while we do gradual roll to remaining zones. Tanya, keep cust_834 in the loop and request lower batch sizes.

tanya-cs: msg sent to account team + customer. They acknowledged and will throttle heavy jobs. No SLA escalation yet.

jon-sre: follow-up actions: - add alert for tenant-level batch-size anomalies - add adaptive backpressure that limits batch_size per-tenant under mem pressure - postmortem owners: runtime + oncall.

sara-oncall: handing over to day oncall @jon-sre in 10m. Current state: degraded -> mitigated, customer notified, config rollback plan ready if needed. I'll remain reachable for questions. :thumbsup:

jon-sre: took handoff. I'll drive the post-incident cleanup (metrics, playbook updates, permanent safeguards).

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Pager cleared.
